the ground using concrete footers the
way we normally would on a job like
this. Instead, we are building two fully
freestanding containment structures —
one behind each goal — that require
no ground penetration whatsoever.
The frames sit on the surface and are
held in place by heavy ballast anchor
weights at each post base. This
approach gives you the same ball-
stopping function as a traditional
backstop while fully respecting the
easement restriction. The structures
can also be repositioned or removed if
needed down the road.
Each structure is built to the following
dimensions: 24 feet wide, 12 feet deep,
and 12 feet tall. The frame is
constructed from 3/4-inch EMT conduit
connected with heavy-duty structural
Kee Klamp fittings and couplings,
which lock together to form a rigid grid
that resists lateral movement and wind
load. The front face of each structure is
left completely open so players and
family members can walk in and out
freely. The back wall, both side panels,
and the full top canopy are covered in
#42 knotted black polyethylene netting
— the same commercial-grade netting
spec we use on our batting cage
builds. This weight and weave will stop
a hard-kicked soccer ball at any

Modern Paver & Turf Layout
This estimate covers the installation of
44 12" x 12" pavers set within a
professional-grade artificial turf inlay.
This specific configuration utilizes a 6"
turf ribbon between each stone,
creating a clean, modern geometric
pattern that balances the structural
stability of masonry with the lush, year-
round green of premium synthetic
grass. This "stepper" style is ideal for
transforming the selected area into a
high-end functional space that
provides superior drainage and a slip-
resistant surface.
The installation process begins with a
standard sub-base excavation and
compaction to ensure the pavers
remain perfectly level over time. Once
the 12" stones are set in their precise
8x5.5 grid (adjusting for the 44-unit
count), the artificial turf is custom-cut
and secured around each individual
paver. This method eliminates the
maintenance associated with natural
grass—such as trimming between
stones or dealing with mud—while
providing a durable, pet-friendly, and
aesthetically striking backyard feature.
